_meta.subject_split_note: SCI (Integrated Science) is Lower Secondary only. BIO, CHEM, PHY are IGCSE only. ENGL (Literature) is IGCSE only. MATH and ENG span both curricula.
_meta.grade_boundary_note: cambridge_lower = Grades 6-8 (Cambridge Stages 7-9). igcse = Grades 9-10 (IGCSE Years 10-11). This overrides the original task file which incorrectly had cambridge_lower = 6-9.
_meta.format_note: Each curriculum_tree entry uses grade_level (singular integer) not grade_levels (array). The seed script must iterate entries individually.
_meta.prerequisite_patch: 2026-03-25: Prerequisites normalised to canonical_codes; 137 cross-grade links added; MATH-ALG-G8-02 wrong prereq removed. Patch authored by Vidhya (curriculum) + Kramer (validation).
_meta.note_on_science: Grade 11/12 Science splits into BIO, CHEM, PHY (same as IGCSE). No 'SCI' subject at AS/A Level.
_meta.note_on_humanities: Geography (GEO), Global Perspectives (GP), History (HIST) are new subjects — add to subjects array.

curricula.name: Cambridge Primary
curricula.description: Cambridge Primary curriculum for Grade 5 (Stage 6). The final year of Cambridge Primary, bridging to Lower Secondary. Covers Mathematics, Integrated Science and English Language.

curricula.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary
curricula.description: Cambridge Lower Secondary curriculum for Grades 6-8 (Stages 7-9). Internationally recognised framework covering Mathematics, Integrated Science and English Language.

curricula.name: Cambridge IGCSE
curricula.description: Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education for Grades 9-10. Externally assessed qualification recognised by universities worldwide.

curricula.name: Cambridge AS & A Level
curricula.description: Cambridge International AS & A Level for Grades 11–12. Externally assessed qualification recognised by universities worldwide as preparation for higher education.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Mathematics covering number, algebra, geometry, statistics and probability.

subjects.name: Integrated Science
subjects.description: Integrated science covering biology, chemistry and physics strands with scientific enquiry. Lower Secondary only.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: English Language covering reading, writing, and speaking and listening.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cambridge IGCSE Biology covering cell biology, physiology, genetics and ecology.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry covering atomic structure, bonding, stoichiometry and organic chemistry.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Cambridge IGCSE Physics covering forces, thermal physics, waves, electricity and nuclear physics.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Cambridge IGCSE English Literature covering poetry, prose and drama.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Cambridge AS & A Level Geography covering physical and human geography, fieldwork and geographical skills.

subjects.name: Global Perspectives
subjects.description: Cambridge AS & A Level Global Perspectives & Research covering critical thinking, stakeholder analysis and independent research.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Cambridge AS & A Level History covering key historical periods, historiography and thematic studies.

topics.name: Number
learning_objectives: Understand place value for integers up to 6 digits and decimals
Work confidently with fractions, decimals and percentages
Solve problems involving ratio and proportion

subtopics.name: Integers and Place Value
subtopics.learning_objective: Read, write, order and compare numbers up to 1,000,000; understand the value of each digit; multiply and divide by 10, 100 and 1000.

subtopics.name: Fractions
subtopics.learning_objective: Compare and order fractions with different denominators; add and subtract fractions including mixed numbers; find fractions of quantities.

subtopics.name: Decimals and Percentages
subtopics.learning_objective: Read, write and order decimals with up to 3 decimal places; convert between fractions, decimals and percentages; calculate simple percentages of whole numbers.

subtopics.name: Multiplication and Division
subtopics.learning_objective: Multiply numbers up to 4 digits by 1 or 2-digit numbers using formal written methods; divide 4-digit numbers by 1-digit numbers; interpret remainders.

subtopics.name: Ratio and Proportion
subtopics.learning_objective: Understand ratio as a comparison of two quantities; write and simplify simple ratios; solve straightforward proportion problems using the unitary method.

topics.name: Algebra
learning_objectives: Recognise and describe number patterns and sequences
Use letters to represent unknowns in simple expressions

subtopics.name: Number Patterns and Sequences
subtopics.learning_objective: Recognise, describe and extend linear number sequences; identify the term-to-term rule; find missing terms in a sequence.

subtopics.name: Simple Expressions and Formulae
subtopics.learning_objective: Use letters to represent unknown quantities in simple expressions; substitute numerical values into simple formulae; describe a simple rule using algebra.

topics.name: Geometry and Measure
learning_objectives: Identify and measure angles; classify 2D and 3D shapes
Calculate perimeter, area and volume of simple shapes
Read and plot coordinates in all four quadrants

subtopics.name: Angles
subtopics.learning_objective: Identify acute, obtuse, right and reflex angles; estimate and measure angles using a protractor; calculate unknown angles on a straight line and around a point.

subtopics.name: 2D and 3D Shapes
subtopics.learning_objective: Name and classify 2D shapes by properties including symmetry; identify faces, edges and vertices of 3D shapes; recognise nets of common 3D shapes.

subtopics.name: Perimeter and Area
subtopics.learning_objective: Calculate the perimeter and area of rectangles and triangles; find the area of compound rectilinear shapes by decomposition.

subtopics.name: Volume and Capacity
subtopics.learning_objective: Calculate the volume of cuboids by counting unit cubes and using the formula l × w × h; convert between units of capacity (ml and l).

subtopics.name: Coordinates and Translation
subtopics.learning_objective: Read and plot coordinates in all four quadrants; describe translations using column vectors; identify and reflect shapes in horizontal and vertical mirror lines.

topics.name: Statistics and Probability
learning_objectives: Collect, organise and represent data in tables and diagrams
Calculate and interpret mean, median, mode and range
Express the probability of simple events

subtopics.name: Data Collection and Graphs
subtopics.learning_objective: Design and use tally charts and frequency tables to collect data; construct and interpret bar charts, line graphs and pie charts from data.

subtopics.name: Mean, Median, Mode and Range
subtopics.learning_objective: Calculate the mean of a data set; identify the median and mode from a list of values; calculate the range; interpret these measures in context.

subtopics.name: Probability
subtopics.learning_objective: Use everyday language (certain, likely, unlikely, impossible) to describe probability; place events on a probability scale from 0 to 1; express probability as a simple fraction.

topics.name: Scientific Enquiry
learning_objectives: Plan simple fair tests and identify variables
Record results accurately and draw simple conclusions

subtopics.name: Planning and Fair Testing
subtopics.learning_objective: Identify what to change, keep the same and measure in a simple investigation; write a prediction; understand what makes a test fair.

subtopics.name: Recording and Concluding
subtopics.learning_objective: Record observations and measurements in tables; display results in bar charts or line graphs; draw conclusions linked to the original prediction.

topics.name: Biology
learning_objectives: Describe the life processes common to living things
Identify the parts of flowering plants and their functions
Describe the main organs of the human body and their roles

subtopics.name: Life Processes and Living Things
subtopics.learning_objective: List and describe the seven life processes (MRS GREN); distinguish between living, dead and never-living things; describe how animals and plants depend on each other.

subtopics.name: Flowering Plants
subtopics.learning_objective: Label the parts of a flowering plant (roots, stem, leaf, flower, fruit, seed); describe the functions of each part; explain pollination and seed dispersal.

subtopics.name: Human Body and Organs
subtopics.learning_objective: Identify the major organs of the human body (heart, lungs, stomach, liver, kidneys, brain); describe the basic function of each organ; understand the role of a balanced diet and exercise.

subtopics.name: Food Chains and Ecosystems
subtopics.learning_objective: Construct and interpret food chains with up to four organisms; identify producers, herbivores, carnivores and omnivores; describe simple interdependence within a habitat.

topics.name: Chemistry
learning_objectives: Describe properties of materials and group them
Explain the three states of matter using particle ideas

subtopics.name: Properties and Uses of Materials
subtopics.learning_objective: Describe and compare the properties of everyday materials (hardness, transparency, flexibility, conductivity); explain why particular materials are chosen for specific uses.

subtopics.name: States of Matter
subtopics.learning_objective: Describe the three states of matter; explain melting, freezing, boiling and condensation; describe the water cycle using the correct scientific vocabulary.

subtopics.name: Mixing and Separating Materials
subtopics.learning_objective: Describe how to separate mixtures using sieving, filtering and evaporation; distinguish between reversible and irreversible changes with examples.

topics.name: Physics
learning_objectives: Describe forces and their effects on objects
Explain how light travels and how shadows are formed
Draw simple circuit diagrams and predict the effect of changes

subtopics.name: Forces
subtopics.learning_objective: Identify gravity, friction, air resistance, water resistance and upthrust; describe how forces affect the speed and direction of objects; measure forces using a newton meter.

subtopics.name: Light and Shadows
subtopics.learning_objective: Explain that light travels in straight lines from a source; describe how shadows are formed and how their size changes; distinguish between transparent, translucent and opaque materials.

subtopics.name: Electricity and Circuits
subtopics.learning_objective: Draw and interpret simple circuit diagrams using standard symbols for battery, bulb, switch and wire; predict the effect of adding or removing components; identify conductors and insulators.

topics.name: Reading
learning_objectives: Retrieve and record explicit information from texts
Make inferences supported by textual evidence
Comment on a writer's use of language

subtopics.name: Reading Comprehension
subtopics.learning_objective: Locate and retrieve explicit information from a range of fiction and non-fiction texts to answer questions; use quotation or close reference to support answers.

subtopics.name: Inference and Deduction
subtopics.learning_objective: Make inferences about character, mood and event from implicit information in a text; explain inferences with reference to specific evidence from the text.

subtopics.name: Language and Vocabulary
subtopics.learning_objective: Identify and comment on a writer's choice of vocabulary and language features including similes, metaphors and personification; explain the effect of these choices on the reader.

topics.name: Writing
learning_objectives: Plan and write for different purposes and audiences
Use a range of sentence structures and punctuation accurately
Write narrative and non-fiction texts with appropriate features

subtopics.name: Writing for Purpose and Audience
subtopics.learning_objective: Plan and write texts for different purposes (to inform, persuade, entertain) and audiences; select appropriate vocabulary, tone and structure.

subtopics.name: Narrative Writing
subtopics.learning_objective: Write stories with a clear structure (beginning, build-up, climax, resolution); use descriptive language, dialogue and varied sentence structures to create character and atmosphere.

subtopics.name: Non-Fiction Writing
subtopics.learning_objective: Write non-fiction texts including instructions, reports and persuasive letters using appropriate layout and language conventions; use headings, bullet points and paragraphs where appropriate.

subtopics.name: Grammar and Punctuation
subtopics.learning_objective: Use a range of punctuation accurately including commas, apostrophes, inverted commas and colons; write in a variety of sentence types (simple, compound, complex); maintain tense consistency.

topics.name: Speaking and Listening
learning_objectives: Listen actively and respond thoughtfully to others
Deliver short presentations with clarity and confidence

subtopics.name: Listening and Responding
subtopics.learning_objective: Listen attentively to others; identify the main points of a spoken text; ask and answer relevant questions; build on the contributions of others in group discussion.

subtopics.name: Speaking and Presentation
subtopics.learning_objective: Deliver a short prepared presentation to a group or class using clear and varied vocabulary, appropriate pace and volume; make eye contact with the audience.

topics.name: Number
learning_objectives: Understand and use place value for integers and decimals
Work with fractions, decimals, percentages and ratio
Solve problems involving proportion

subtopics.name: Integers and Place Value
subtopics.learning_objective: Understand the value of each digit in integers up to 7 digits; order and compare positive and negative integers on a number line.

subtopics.name: Fractions
subtopics.learning_objective: Compare and order fractions; convert between improper fractions and mixed numbers; calculate fractions of whole number quantities.

subtopics.name: Decimals and Percentages
subtopics.learning_objective: Convert fluently between fractions, decimals and percentages; calculate simple percentages of quantities and express one quantity as a percentage of another.

subtopics.name: Ratio and Proportion
subtopics.learning_objective: Write and simplify ratios; divide a quantity into a given ratio; solve simple proportion problems using the unitary method.

topics.name: Algebra
learning_objectives: Recognise and describe number patterns and sequences
Use letters to represent unknowns and write algebraic expressions
Solve simple linear equations

subtopics.name: Sequences
subtopics.learning_objective: Recognise and extend linear and simple non-linear sequences; describe the term-to-term rule in words and using algebra.

subtopics.name: Algebraic Expressions
subtopics.learning_objective: Write and simplify algebraic expressions; substitute numerical values into expressions and formulae to evaluate them.

subtopics.name: Simple Linear Equations
subtopics.learning_objective: Form and solve one-step and two-step linear equations with the unknown on one side, including equations arising from problem contexts.

topics.name: Geometry and Measure
learning_objectives: Identify and calculate angles in 2D shapes and on straight lines
Classify and describe properties of 2D and 3D shapes
Calculate area, perimeter and convert between metric units

subtopics.name: Angles and Lines
subtopics.learning_objective: Identify acute, obtuse, reflex and right angles; calculate unknown angles on a straight line, at a point, and in triangles and quadrilaterals.

subtopics.name: 2D Shape Properties
subtopics.learning_objective: Classify triangles by side length and angle; classify quadrilaterals by their properties; identify lines of symmetry and the order of rotational symmetry.

subtopics.name: Area and Perimeter
subtopics.learning_objective: Calculate the perimeter and area of rectangles, triangles, parallelograms and compound rectilinear shapes; solve problems in context.

subtopics.name: Units and Measurement
subtopics.learning_objective: Convert between metric units of length, mass and capacity; read scales accurately; estimate and measure lengths, masses and capacities.

topics.name: Statistics and Probability
learning_objectives: Collect, organise and represent data in appropriate diagrams
Calculate and interpret measures of average and spread
Express and calculate probability of simple events

subtopics.name: Data Representation
subtopics.learning_objective: Construct and interpret bar charts, pictograms, line graphs and simple pie charts from frequency tables and raw data.

subtopics.name: Averages and Range
subtopics.learning_objective: Calculate the mean, median, mode and range from a set of raw data; interpret and compare these measures in context.

subtopics.name: Probability Scale
subtopics.learning_objective: Describe the likelihood of events using probability language; express the probability of a single event as a fraction, decimal or percentage on a 0-to-1 scale.

topics.name: Number
learning_objectives: Perform calculations with fractions, decimals and percentages
Apply index notation and calculate powers and roots
Express numbers in standard form and solve proportion problems

subtopics.name: Fractions, Decimals and Percentages
subtopics.learning_objective: Perform the four operations with fractions and decimals; calculate percentage increase and decrease; express percentage change.

subtopics.name: Powers and Roots
subtopics.learning_objective: Calculate squares, square roots, cubes and cube roots; use index notation; apply the rules of indices for positive integer exponents.

subtopics.name: Standard Form
subtopics.learning_objective: Express large and small numbers in standard form (a × 10ⁿ where 1 ≤ a < 10); convert between standard form and ordinary numbers.

subtopics.name: Ratio and Direct Proportion
subtopics.learning_objective: Solve problems using ratio, including sharing in a given ratio; recognise and use direct proportion; construct and use proportion equations.

topics.name: Algebra
learning_objectives: Expand and factorise algebraic expressions
Solve linear equations and inequalities
Plot and interpret linear graphs

subtopics.name: Algebraic Manipulation
subtopics.learning_objective: Expand single brackets and simplify algebraic expressions; factorise expressions by extracting a common factor.

subtopics.name: Linear Equations
subtopics.learning_objective: Solve linear equations with unknowns on both sides and those involving brackets; form equations from word problems and check solutions.

subtopics.name: Inequalities
subtopics.learning_objective: Write, solve and represent linear inequalities on a number line; use correct inequality notation including strict and non-strict inequalities.

subtopics.name: Linear Graphs
subtopics.learning_objective: Plot and interpret graphs of linear functions; identify gradient and y-intercept from the equation y = mx + c; find the equation of a line from its graph.

topics.name: Geometry and Measure
learning_objectives: Apply Pythagoras theorem to right-angled triangles
Calculate area and volume of circles and 3D shapes
Perform and describe geometric transformations

subtopics.name: Pythagoras' Theorem
subtopics.learning_objective: State and apply Pythagoras' theorem to calculate the length of unknown sides in right-angled triangles; determine whether a triangle is right-angled.

subtopics.name: Circles — Area and Circumference
subtopics.learning_objective: Calculate the circumference and area of circles and semicircles; solve problems involving circles in real-world contexts.

subtopics.name: Volume and Surface Area
subtopics.learning_objective: Calculate the volume and surface area of cuboids, triangular prisms and cylinders; solve problems in context.

subtopics.name: Transformations
subtopics.learning_objective: Perform and describe rotations, reflections, translations and enlargements on a coordinate grid; identify properties preserved under each transformation.

topics.name: Statistics and Probability
learning_objectives: Construct and interpret a wider range of statistical diagrams
Calculate statistics from grouped data
Calculate probabilities of combined events

subtopics.name: Statistical Diagrams
subtopics.learning_objective: Construct and interpret scatter diagrams, stem-and-leaf diagrams and frequency polygons; describe correlation and identify outliers.

subtopics.name: Averages from Grouped Data
subtopics.learning_objective: Estimate the mean from a grouped frequency table; identify the modal class and the class containing the median; compare distributions.

subtopics.name: Combined Event Probability
subtopics.learning_objective: List outcomes systematically using sample space diagrams; calculate probabilities of combined events; apply P(A) + P(not A) = 1.

topics.name: Number
learning_objectives: Simplify and use surds
Apply direct and inverse proportion
Calculate compound measures

subtopics.name: Surds
subtopics.learning_objective: Simplify surds; add, subtract and multiply expressions involving surds; rationalise a denominator of the form √n.

subtopics.name: Proportional Reasoning
subtopics.learning_objective: Apply direct and inverse proportion to multi-step problems; recognise and construct graphs of direct and inverse proportion.

subtopics.name: Compound Measures
subtopics.learning_objective: Calculate speed, density and pressure using the correct formulae; convert between compound units; choose appropriate units for a given context.

topics.name: Algebra
learning_objectives: Expand and factorise quadratic expressions
Solve simultaneous linear equations
Use function notation and find nth terms

subtopics.name: Quadratic Expressions
subtopics.learning_objective: Expand the product of two binomials; factorise quadratic expressions of the form x² + bx + c; recognise the difference of two squares.

subtopics.name: Simultaneous Equations
subtopics.learning_objective: Solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations using the elimination and substitution methods; interpret solutions graphically.

subtopics.name: Functions
subtopics.learning_objective: Understand and use function notation f(x); find outputs for given inputs; identify the domain and range of simple functions.

subtopics.name: Nth Term of Sequences
subtopics.learning_objective: Derive and use the nth term formula for arithmetic sequences; determine whether a given value is a term in a sequence.

topics.name: Geometry and Measure
learning_objectives: Use trigonometric ratios in right-angled triangles
Apply circle properties
Use similarity and enlargement to find unknown lengths

subtopics.name: Trigonometric Ratios
subtopics.learning_objective: Define and use sine, cosine and tangent ratios to calculate unknown sides and angles in right-angled triangles in 2D contexts.

subtopics.name: Circle Properties
subtopics.learning_objective: Apply the properties of tangents, chords and the angle in a semicircle; calculate arc length and sector area as fractions of a full circle.

subtopics.name: Similarity and Enlargement
subtopics.learning_objective: Identify similar figures; use scale factors to find unknown lengths, areas and volumes in similar shapes; perform enlargements with fractional scale factors.

topics.name: Statistics and Probability
learning_objectives: Construct and interpret cumulative frequency graphs and histograms
Calculate probabilities using tree diagrams

subtopics.name: Cumulative Frequency
subtopics.learning_objective: Construct and use cumulative frequency tables and graphs; estimate the median, lower and upper quartiles, and interquartile range.

subtopics.name: Histograms
subtopics.learning_objective: Draw and interpret histograms with unequal class widths using frequency density; calculate frequencies from a histogram.

subtopics.name: Tree Diagrams and Combined Probability
subtopics.learning_objective: Construct and use tree diagrams to calculate the probability of two or more combined independent and dependent events.

topics.name: Scientific Enquiry
learning_objectives: Plan and carry out fair scientific investigations
Record and present scientific data accurately

subtopics.name: Planning Investigations
subtopics.learning_objective: Identify independent, dependent and control variables in a scientific investigation; write a testable hypothesis and design a fair test.

subtopics.name: Recording and Presenting Data
subtopics.learning_objective: Select appropriate apparatus; record results accurately in clearly labelled tables; present data as bar charts and line graphs, choosing appropriate scales.

topics.name: Biology
learning_objectives: Identify and describe the structure of plant and animal cells
Explain photosynthesis and the role of producers
Describe food chains, food webs and the roles of organisms in ecosystems

subtopics.name: Cells and Cell Functions
subtopics.learning_objective: Identify and label the structures of plant and animal cells; state the function of the nucleus, cell membrane, cytoplasm, cell wall, vacuole and chloroplasts.

subtopics.name: Photosynthesis
subtopics.learning_objective: Write the word equation for photosynthesis; describe the roles of light, chlorophyll, carbon dioxide and water; explain why plants are producers in a food chain.

subtopics.name: Ecosystems and Food Chains
subtopics.learning_objective: Construct and interpret food chains and food webs; describe the roles of producers, consumers and decomposers; explain energy flow through a food chain.

topics.name: Chemistry
learning_objectives: Describe the arrangement and movement of particles in the three states of matter
Distinguish between elements, compounds and mixtures and describe separation methods
Compare the physical properties of common materials

subtopics.name: States of Matter
subtopics.learning_objective: Describe the arrangement and movement of particles in solids, liquids and gases; explain melting, boiling, condensation and freezing in terms of particle theory.

subtopics.name: Mixtures and Separation Techniques
subtopics.learning_objective: Distinguish between elements, compounds and mixtures using particle diagrams; describe and explain filtration, evaporation, distillation and chromatography.

subtopics.name: Properties of Materials
subtopics.learning_objective: Compare physical properties including hardness, solubility, thermal and electrical conductivity; explain material selection for specific uses based on properties.

topics.name: Physics
learning_objectives: Identify forces and describe their effects on motion
Describe energy forms and energy transfer
Draw and interpret simple electric circuits

subtopics.name: Forces and Their Effects
subtopics.learning_objective: Identify contact and non-contact forces; describe the effects of balanced and unbalanced forces on the motion and shape of objects.

subtopics.name: Energy Forms and Transfer
subtopics.learning_objective: Identify different forms of energy (kinetic, potential, thermal, chemical, electrical, light, sound); describe energy transfers and transformations in everyday contexts.

subtopics.name: Electric Circuits
subtopics.learning_objective: Draw and interpret circuit diagrams using standard symbols; describe the difference between series and parallel circuits; predict the effect of adding components.

topics.name: Scientific Enquiry
learning_objectives: Evaluate validity and reliability of investigations
Draw evidence-based conclusions

subtopics.name: Variables and Fair Testing
subtopics.learning_objective: Distinguish between independent, dependent and control variables; evaluate the validity and reliability of an investigation design.

subtopics.name: Analysing Evidence and Drawing Conclusions
subtopics.learning_objective: Identify patterns and anomalies in data; draw conclusions based on evidence; relate findings to scientific knowledge and suggest explanations.

topics.name: Biology
learning_objectives: Describe the structure and function of key human organ systems
Explain reproduction in plants and humans
Identify the components of a balanced diet and their roles

subtopics.name: Human Organ Systems
subtopics.learning_objective: Describe the structure and function of the digestive, circulatory and respiratory systems; explain how these systems interact to sustain life.

subtopics.name: Reproduction
subtopics.learning_objective: Compare sexual and asexual reproduction; describe fertilisation in plants and humans; explain the stages of the menstrual cycle.

subtopics.name: Nutrition and Health
subtopics.learning_objective: Identify the roles of carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals and water in the diet; explain the effects of nutritional deficiency and excess on health.

topics.name: Chemistry
learning_objectives: Describe atomic structure and use the Periodic Table
Distinguish between physical and chemical changes
Describe acids, alkalis and neutralisation

subtopics.name: Atoms, Elements and the Periodic Table
subtopics.learning_objective: Describe the structure of the atom in terms of protons, neutrons and electrons; use the Periodic Table to identify element properties and group trends.

subtopics.name: Chemical and Physical Changes
subtopics.learning_objective: Distinguish between physical and chemical changes with examples; write word equations for combustion, oxidation and neutralisation reactions.

subtopics.name: Acids, Alkalis and Neutralisation
subtopics.learning_objective: Use the pH scale to classify substances as acidic, neutral or alkaline; describe the reaction between acids and bases; use indicators to determine pH.

topics.name: Physics
learning_objectives: Describe reflection and refraction of light with ray diagrams
Explain the properties and transmission of sound
Describe the structure of the solar system and celestial motion

subtopics.name: Light and Optics
subtopics.learning_objective: Describe reflection and refraction using ray diagrams; explain how lenses form images; describe dispersion of white light into a spectrum.

subtopics.name: Sound and Waves
subtopics.learning_objective: Describe how sound is produced and transmitted as a longitudinal wave; relate pitch to frequency and loudness to amplitude; explain echoes and uses of ultrasound.

subtopics.name: Earth and Space
subtopics.learning_objective: Describe the structure of the solar system; explain day and night, seasons and lunar phases using models of the Earth's and Moon's motion.

topics.name: Scientific Enquiry
learning_objectives: Evaluate the quality of evidence and suggest improvements to experimental design

subtopics.name: Evaluating Investigations
subtopics.learning_objective: Evaluate the quality of evidence by identifying sources of systematic and random error; suggest improvements to experimental design to increase reliability and validity.

topics.name: Biology
learning_objectives: Explain inheritance using DNA and Punnett squares
Describe how pathogens cause disease and how the body responds
Compare aerobic and anaerobic respiration

subtopics.name: Genetics and Inheritance
subtopics.learning_objective: Describe the structure of DNA and the role of genes in inheritance; use Punnett squares to predict ratios of offspring phenotypes for a single trait.

subtopics.name: Disease and Immunity
subtopics.learning_objective: Classify pathogens as bacteria, viruses, fungi and protists; describe modes of transmission; explain how the immune system responds and how vaccination prevents disease.

subtopics.name: Respiration and Gas Exchange
subtopics.learning_objective: Write word equations for aerobic and anaerobic respiration; compare the two processes; describe the structure of the lungs and explain gas exchange across the alveoli.

topics.name: Chemistry
learning_objectives: Describe Periodic Table trends and reactivity
Explain rates of reaction using collision theory
Describe reversible reactions

subtopics.name: The Periodic Table and Reactivity
subtopics.learning_objective: Describe the trends in reactivity in Group 1 and Group 7; explain reactivity using electron configuration; write displacement reaction equations.

subtopics.name: Rates of Reaction
subtopics.learning_objective: State and explain the effect of concentration, temperature, surface area and catalysts on reaction rate; use collision theory to explain these effects.

subtopics.name: Reversible Reactions
subtopics.learning_objective: Describe reversible reactions with examples such as hydration of copper sulfate; explain what happens to products and reactants when the reaction is reversed.

topics.name: Physics
learning_objectives: Describe electromagnetism and its applications
Define wave properties and calculate wave speed
Apply Newton's laws to explain motion

subtopics.name: Electromagnetism
subtopics.learning_objective: Describe the magnetic field around a current-carrying conductor; explain how an electromagnet works; name applications including electric motors and relays.

subtopics.name: Wave Properties
subtopics.learning_objective: Define amplitude, frequency, wavelength and wave speed; calculate wave speed using v = fλ; distinguish between transverse and longitudinal waves.

subtopics.name: Forces and Motion
subtopics.learning_objective: Interpret distance-time and velocity-time graphs; calculate speed, acceleration and distance; state and apply Newton's First, Second and Third Laws.

topics.name: Reading
learning_objectives: Retrieve and interpret explicit and implicit information from texts
Analyse language and structural features

subtopics.name: Reading for Explicit Meaning
subtopics.learning_objective: Retrieve and select relevant explicit information from fiction and non-fiction texts to answer questions, using direct quotation or close paraphrase.

subtopics.name: Inference and Deduction
subtopics.learning_objective: Make inferences about character, mood and situation from implicit information in a text; support inferences with specific evidence.

subtopics.name: Language and Structure Analysis
subtopics.learning_objective: Identify and comment on a writer's language choices including figurative language, word choice and structural techniques, explaining their effects on the reader.

topics.name: Writing
learning_objectives: Write for different purposes and audiences
Write narrative and non-fiction texts with appropriate features

subtopics.name: Writing for Purpose and Audience
subtopics.learning_objective: Plan and write texts for different purposes (inform, entertain, persuade) and audiences; select appropriate tone, register and vocabulary.

subtopics.name: Narrative Writing
subtopics.learning_objective: Write engaging stories and descriptions using varied sentence structures, effective vocabulary, dialogue and imagery to create character and atmosphere.

subtopics.name: Non-Fiction Writing

subtopics.learning_objective: Use sine, cosine and tangent for any angle; apply the sine and cosine rules; use identities including sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 and double angle formulae; solve trigonometric equations.

subtopics.name: Logarithms and Exponentials
subtopics.learning_objective: Understand and use exponential growth and decay; work with natural logarithms; apply the laws of logarithms; convert between exponential and logarithmic forms.

topics.name: Mechanics
learning_objectives: Model motion in one and two dimensions using kinematics equations
Apply Newton's laws to particles in equilibrium and motion
Calculate work, energy and power in mechanical systems

subtopics.name: Kinematics and Dynamics
subtopics.learning_objective: Apply equations of uniform acceleration in one and two dimensions; use velocity-time graphs; model projectile motion; apply Newton's second law to connected particles.

subtopics.name: Forces and Equilibrium
subtopics.learning_objective: Resolve forces in two dimensions; apply conditions for static equilibrium; analyse friction forces; solve problems involving connected particles on inclined planes.

subtopics.name: Work, Energy and Power
subtopics.learning_objective: Calculate work done by constant and variable forces; apply the work-energy theorem; use the principle of conservation of energy; calculate power and efficiency.

topics.name: Statistics
learning_objectives: Calculate and interpret measures of location and spread for grouped and ungrouped data
Use probability distributions including binomial and normal
Conduct hypothesis tests for population parameters

subtopics.name: Probability and Distributions
subtopics.learning_objective: Calculate probabilities using addition and multiplication rules; use binomial and normal distributions; find probabilities and critical values from tables and calculators.

subtopics.name: Hypothesis Testing
subtopics.learning_objective: Formulate null and alternative hypotheses; conduct one-tailed and two-tailed tests for a population proportion using the binomial distribution; interpret p-values and critical regions.

topics.name: Pure Mathematics
learning_objectives: Extend algebraic skills to complex numbers, further calculus and differential equations
Apply vectors and matrices to geometric and algebraic problems

subtopics.name: Advanced Calculus and Differential Equations
subtopics.learning_objective: Integrate using substitution, by parts and partial fractions; solve first and second order differential equations; apply calculus to volumes of revolution and parametric equations.

subtopics.name: Complex Numbers
subtopics.learning_objective: Perform arithmetic with complex numbers in Cartesian and modulus-argument form; represent complex numbers on an Argand diagram; find roots of polynomial equations with complex roots.

subtopics.name: Further Algebra and Functions
subtopics.learning_objective: Use the binomial theorem for rational and negative exponents; apply partial fractions; work with parametric equations; understand proof by induction.

subtopics.name: Vectors and Matrices
subtopics.learning_objective: Perform vector operations in 3D; find equations of lines and planes; multiply matrices; find determinants and inverse matrices; solve systems of linear equations.

topics.name: Mechanics
learning_objectives: Analyse circular motion and oscillations
Apply advanced energy and momentum principles

subtopics.name: Advanced Kinematics and Circular Motion
subtopics.learning_objective: Analyse motion in a circle with constant speed; calculate centripetal acceleration and force; apply kinematics using calculus (variable acceleration); model simple harmonic motion.

subtopics.name: Energy, Work and Mechanical Systems
subtopics.learning_objective: Apply the work-energy principle to variable forces; analyse elastic strings and springs using Hooke's law; use the impulse-momentum theorem; model mechanical systems with energy methods.

topics.name: Statistics
learning_objectives: Apply advanced probability distributions
Conduct and interpret a range of hypothesis tests
Carry out statistical investigations and present findings critically

subtopics.name: Advanced Probability Distributions
subtopics.learning_objective: Use Poisson, geometric and normal distributions; apply the central limit theorem; calculate confidence intervals for population means; work with continuous random variables and probability density functions.

subtopics.name: Advanced Hypothesis Testing
subtopics.learning_objective: Conduct hypothesis tests for population means using the normal and t-distributions; test for correlation; carry out chi-squared tests for goodness of fit and independence.

subtopics.name: Statistical Investigation and Reporting
subtopics.learning_objective: Plan, carry out and critically evaluate a statistical investigation; select appropriate tests; present findings with correct interpretation of results, confidence intervals and limitations.

topics.name: Biochemistry and Cell Biology
learning_objectives: Describe the structure and function of biological molecules
Explain enzyme kinetics and metabolic pathways
Describe cellular respiration and photosynthesis at a biochemical level

subtopics.name: Biochemistry and Metabolism
subtopics.learning_objective: Describe the structure of carbohydrates, lipids, proteins and nucleic acids; explain metabolic pathways including glycolysis, the Krebs cycle and oxidative phosphorylation; describe the role of ATP in energy transfer.

subtopics.name: DNA, Genes and Protein Synthesis
subtopics.learning_objective: Describe the structure of DNA and RNA; explain transcription and translation in detail; describe gene expression and its regulation; explain the principles of genetic engineering and PCR.

subtopics.name: Plant and Animal Physiology
subtopics.learning_objective: Describe gas exchange in plants, fish, insects and mammals; explain thermoregulation; describe the structure and function of the mammalian kidney in excretion and osmoregulation.

subtopics.name: Ecology and Conservation
subtopics.learning_objective: Describe population growth models; explain factors affecting population size; describe energy flow through ecosystems; evaluate conservation strategies and the impact of human activity on biodiversity.

topics.name: Advanced Biology
learning_objectives: Apply knowledge of genetics, genomics and biotechnology to current research
Analyse physiological systems at advanced level
Evaluate ecological data and conservation issues

subtopics.name: Genomics and Biotechnology
subtopics.learning_objective: Explain the principles of genomics and gene sequencing; describe the applications of recombinant DNA technology; evaluate the ethical implications of genetic modification and cloning.

subtopics.name: Physiology and Health Science
subtopics.learning_objective: Describe the control of heart rate and ventilation; explain the immune response in detail including cell-mediated and humoral immunity; evaluate the physiology of exercise and disease.

subtopics.name: Ecosystem Analysis
subtopics.learning_objective: Analyse ecosystems using quantitative techniques; evaluate succession and climax communities; interpret population data; discuss global issues including climate change and biodiversity loss.

subtopics.name: Research in Life Sciences
subtopics.learning_objective: Design and evaluate biological investigations; apply statistical analysis to biological data; critically evaluate published research; present findings in scientific report format.

topics.name: Advanced Chemistry
learning_objectives: Describe atomic structure, bonding and energetics at advanced level
Explain reaction kinetics and equilibrium quantitatively
Apply organic chemistry to functional group reactions

subtopics.name: Atomic Structure and Bonding
subtopics.learning_objective: Describe atomic orbitals and electron configuration; explain ionic, covalent, metallic and intermolecular bonding in detail; predict molecular shapes using VSEPR theory; describe lattice structures.

subtopics.name: Energetics and Kinetics
subtopics.learning_objective: Calculate enthalpy changes using Hess's law and bond energies; apply collision theory and Arrhenius equation to reaction rates; describe the effect of catalysts on activation energy.

subtopics.name: Acids, Bases and Equilibrium
subtopics.learning_objective: Apply Brønsted-Lowry theory to acid-base reactions; calculate pH and Ka; describe buffer action; apply Le Chatelier's principle and Kc to equilibrium calculations.

topics.name: Advanced Chemistry
learning_objectives: Apply spectroscopic techniques to identify organic compounds
Evaluate contemporary chemical research and applications

subtopics.name: Spectroscopy and Analysis
subtopics.learning_objective: Interpret mass spectra, IR, NMR and UV-Vis spectra to identify organic compounds; use chromatography for separation and identification; evaluate analytical data from multiple techniques.

subtopics.name: Chemical Research and Applications
subtopics.learning_objective: Evaluate industrial chemical processes including the Haber and Contact processes; discuss green chemistry principles; design and evaluate synthetic routes for organic molecules; assess environmental impact.

topics.name: Advanced Physics
learning_objectives: Apply advanced mechanics including circular motion and oscillations
Describe thermal physics and thermodynamic principles
Analyse waves, optics and the electromagnetic spectrum quantitatively

subtopics.name: Mechanics and Motion
subtopics.learning_objective: Apply Newton's laws to circular motion, rotation and oscillation; analyse simple harmonic motion mathematically; use conservation of energy and momentum in multi-body collisions.

subtopics.name: Thermal Physics
subtopics.learning_objective: Apply the ideal gas laws and kinetic theory; calculate internal energy, heat and work done in thermodynamic processes; describe the first and second laws of thermodynamics.

subtopics.name: Waves and Oscillations
subtopics.learning_objective: Describe stationary and progressive waves; explain diffraction, interference and polarisation; apply superposition to double-slit and diffraction grating experiments; describe the Doppler effect.

subtopics.name: Electricity and Magnetism
subtopics.learning_objective: Apply Kirchhoff's laws to complex circuits; describe the behaviour of capacitors in DC circuits; explain the magnetic force on moving charges and current-carrying conductors; describe electromagnetic induction quantitatively.

topics.name: Advanced Physics
learning_objectives: Describe quantum physics and the wave-particle duality
Apply electromagnetic theory to advanced contexts
Explain nuclear and particle physics

subtopics.name: Quantum Physics
subtopics.learning_objective: Describe the photoelectric effect and photon model; explain wave-particle duality and de Broglie wavelength; describe atomic energy levels, emission and absorption spectra; apply the uncertainty principle.

subtopics.name: Electromagnetic Theory
subtopics.learning_objective: Apply Faraday's and Lenz's laws to electromagnetic induction; describe alternating current circuits including capacitors and inductors; explain the operation of transformers and AC generators quantitatively.

subtopics.name: Nuclear and Particle Physics
subtopics.learning_objective: Describe nuclear stability, binding energy and mass defect; explain fission and fusion; describe fundamental particles and the quark model; apply conservation laws to particle interactions.

subtopics.name: Scientific Investigation and Reporting
subtopics.learning_objective: Plan and execute advanced experimental investigations; identify and minimise sources of error; evaluate results statistically; write a formal scientific report with critical analysis of methodology and findings.

topics.name: Reading
learning_objectives: Analyse texts for meaning, style, context and argument
Compare literary forms across prose, poetry and drama

subtopics.name: Advanced Textual Analysis
subtopics.learning_objective: Analyse unseen texts for meaning, style, context and argument; evaluate a writer's rhetorical strategies; compare how different literary forms — prose, poetry and drama — achieve effects.

subtopics.name: Argument and Rhetoric
subtopics.learning_objective: Evaluate the structure and persuasiveness of argument in non-literary texts; identify rhetorical devices and assess their effectiveness; compare viewpoints across multiple sources.

topics.name: Writing
learning_objectives: Write critical, comparative and interpretive essays with sustained argument
Develop a consistent and distinctive writing style

subtopics.name: Critical and Comparative Writing
subtopics.learning_objective: Write sustained critical, comparative and interpretive essays; construct and develop a coherent argument with embedded evidence; maintain a consistent analytical register throughout extended writing.

subtopics.name: Research and Documentation
subtopics.learning_objective: Plan and conduct textual research; select, evaluate and synthesise sources; reference accurately using a recognised system; integrate secondary material into original analytical writing.

subtopics.name: Style and Voice
subtopics.learning_objective: Develop a distinctive and effective writing style; adapt register and tone for different purposes; demonstrate control of sentence structure, vocabulary and stylistic devices in original writing.

topics.name: Speaking and Listening
learning_objectives: Deliver a thesis-level presentation and respond to questions
Participate in and lead formal academic discussion

subtopics.name: Thesis Presentation and Panel Discussion
subtopics.learning_objective: Deliver a structured academic presentation on a chosen thesis; respond to audience questions with evidence and analysis; participate in and manage panel and group discussion with sustained engagement.

topics.name: Reading
learning_objectives: Conduct advanced literary analysis across multiple texts
Synthesise argument and critical perspective at university-entry level

subtopics.name: Advanced Literary Analysis
subtopics.learning_objective: Produce advanced literary analysis demonstrating awareness of literary theory, historical context and intertextuality; evaluate a writer's craft with sustained critical perspective across extended texts.

subtopics.name: Comparative Study and Synthesis
subtopics.learning_objective: Compare and synthesise argument, viewpoint and critical perspective across multiple texts and secondary sources; produce a coherent, evidence-based analytical response at university-entry level.

topics.name: Writing
learning_objectives: Write extended analytical essays at university-entry standard
Produce professional and research-based writing

subtopics.name: Extended Analytical Essay
subtopics.learning_objective: Write extended analytical essays at university-entry standard; sustain a sophisticated argument with precise use of textual evidence; demonstrate command of academic register and critical vocabulary.

subtopics.name: Research, Documentation and Professional Writing
subtopics.learning_objective: Conduct independent textual research; write for professional and academic contexts including reports, proposals and reflective commentaries; apply accurate referencing and academic conventions throughout.

topics.name: Speaking and Listening
learning_objectives: Lead seminars and defend scholarship orally
Critically analyse media and spoken texts

subtopics.name: Seminar Leadership and Oral Defence
subtopics.learning_objective: Lead academic seminars with authority and responsiveness; defend a scholarly argument under questioning; critically analyse spoken and media texts for bias, rhetoric and purpose.

topics.name: Physical and Human Geography
learning_objectives: Explain physical processes including tectonics, hydrology and climate
Analyse human geography including globalisation and urban development

subtopics.name: Physical Geography
subtopics.learning_objective: Explain tectonic processes, glaciation and coastal systems; describe the hydrological cycle and river processes; analyse the causes and impacts of natural hazards; interpret OS maps and satellite images.

subtopics.name: Human Geography and Globalisation
subtopics.learning_objective: Analyse the causes and consequences of globalisation; describe patterns of migration, urbanisation and development; evaluate the impact of transnational corporations and international trade on development.

topics.name: Advanced Geography
learning_objectives: Conduct geographical fieldwork and research
Evaluate political, urban and environmental geographical issues

subtopics.name: Fieldwork and Geographical Research
subtopics.learning_objective: Design and conduct geographical fieldwork; collect, process and analyse primary and secondary data; evaluate methodology and present findings as a structured geographical investigation.

subtopics.name: Political, Urban and Environmental Geography
subtopics.learning_objective: Evaluate political geography including borders, governance and supranational organisations; analyse urban regeneration and sustainability; assess responses to environmental challenges including climate change.

topics.name: Global Perspectives and Research
learning_objectives: Apply critical thinking to global issues from multiple perspectives
Conduct independent research and present findings

subtopics.name: Stakeholder Analysis and Critical Thinking
subtopics.learning_objective: Identify and analyse the perspectives of stakeholders on a global issue; evaluate the credibility and bias of sources; apply critical thinking frameworks to construct a reasoned argument.

subtopics.name: International Research Projects
subtopics.learning_objective: Plan and conduct an international research project on a global issue; gather and synthesise evidence from diverse sources; collaborate with peers to produce a team essay and reflective portfolio.

topics.name: Advanced Global Perspectives
learning_objectives: Produce an independent capstone research project on a global challenge
Apply theory to global challenges and present at advanced level

subtopics.name: Capstone Research Project
subtopics.learning_objective: Produce an independent research project on a self-chosen global issue; apply theoretical frameworks; synthesise evidence from multiple perspectives; write a formal research report with bibliography.

subtopics.name: Theory and Application to Global Challenges
subtopics.learning_objective: Apply social science theory to contemporary global challenges; evaluate policy responses to issues such as climate change, inequality and migration; present conclusions in an academic debate format.

topics.name: Historical Study
learning_objectives: Analyse key historical periods using primary and secondary sources
Apply historiographical approaches to historical evidence

subtopics.name: In-Depth Study of Historical Periods
subtopics.learning_objective: Analyse a chosen historical period using primary and secondary sources; evaluate the significance of key events, individuals and turning points; construct an evidence-based historical argument.

subtopics.name: Thematic and Historiographical Studies
subtopics.learning_objective: Analyse historical themes across time periods (war, society, technology, power); evaluate the perspectives of different historians; explain how interpretations of history change over time.

topics.name: Advanced Historical Study
learning_objectives: Conduct comparative historical studies across cultures and periods
Apply historiographical methodology to independent research

subtopics.name: Comparative Historical Studies
subtopics.learning_objective: Compare historical developments across different societies, cultures and time periods; evaluate the extent to which historical patterns repeat; produce a comparative analytical essay with source evaluation.

subtopics.name: Historiography and Methodology
subtopics.learning_objective: Apply and evaluate major historiographical schools (Marxist, feminist, postcolonial, revisionist); conduct independent archival or source-based research; present an extended historical argument with full scholarly apparatus.

subtopics.name: Modern and Ancient Cultures
subtopics.learning_objective: Explore the interaction between ancient and modern cultures; analyse cultural transmission, syncretism and colonialism; evaluate the legacy of historical periods on contemporary society.
